Not covered by provided measurements (cells_measured=235 for whole well, no DMSO median given).

Tubulin (green) mean intensity, variance and texture strongly increased vs DMSO filamentous network: dense bright perinuclear bundles, rings and clumps encircling nuclei, heterogeneous clumped staining vs faint radial microtubules in control.

F-actin (red) mean intensity and variance increased vs control thin cortex: prominent thick peripheral ruffles/lamellipodia and circumferential bands around enlarged cells; controls show faint diffuse stress fibers.

DNA (blue in composite, appears pale blue in DMSO vs bright yellow/white in treated due to very high intensity + overlap) nuclei enlarged, irregular contour, reduced solidity/form-factor; frequent multilobed/horseshoe shapes vs smooth oval single nuclei in DMSO.
Increased multinucleation: many cells contain 2- >5 closely apposed distinct DAPI foci (yellow dots) or fragmented nuclei within shared cytoplasm, vs ~20% bi-nucleate baseline in control.
Average cell footprint increased, flattened and spread with aberrant mitotic-like arrest morphology. Not directly covered by provided measurements.

notable_cells.why: Large spread cell with dense green tubulin bundle ring around irregular multinucleate center and thick red actin rim - exemplifies tub_mean/tub_std/glcm increase and nuc solidity loss

candidate_mechanisms.why: Extreme tubulin gain-of-signal z=42.8 mean, 75.1 std, 59.5 contrast indicates polymer stabilization/bundling, not loss; associated mitotic failure, enlarged irregular nuclei (solidity z=-33.2, form_factor z=-18.1) and multinucleation (z=13.5) and compensatory cortical actin increase (z=41.3). Opposite to destabilizers which decrease tubulin polymer.

report.uncertainty: Composite-only, no grayscale DNA/tubulin/actin channels; nuclear intensity inferred from blue->yellow shift in merge. Actin increase may be secondary to cell spreading/arrest rather than direct actin targeting, but Aurora/Eg5 inhibitors can also give multinucleation without such extreme tubulin bundling, so stabilizer favored with medium-high confidence.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as taxol (PubChem CID 36314, ChEMBL CHEMBL428647, curated as Tubulin inhibitor e13/e14) - verdict correct: Microtubule stabilizers 0.94, truth Microtubule stabilizers. This aligns with established taxol mechanism of microtubule stabilization PMID 7865431 and taxane-binding pocket literature PMID 39496813, and fluorescent taxoid work PMID 9000007 in this run, without needing new clinical inference.

What got it right:
- Acquisition strategy: after list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.001-3 µM with 4 wells accessible (e1), we sampled extremes and mid-range: 3 µM (e2), 0.03 µM (e3), 0.001 µM (e6), 0.3 µM (e7). All four independent wells showed massive, directionally consistent tubulin gain: tub_std z=+75.1, +56.4, +74.7 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+59.6, +56.4, +65.5 and tub_mean z=+42.8, +43.9, +46.0 (e2,e3,e7). Even the lowest dose 0.001 µM already had tub_std z=+13.8 (e6) with nuc_solidity z=-13.3, indicating potent bundling/morphology change at threshold and saturation thereafter. The magnitude (z +40 to +75) is far beyond assay noise and opposite to what destabilizers predict.
- Visual confirmation: describe_phenotype on 4 fields (e4) noted lower density vs DMSO and independently nominated Microtubule stabilizers with 6 observations, converging with quantitative features.
- Atlas comparison: NSC vote 2/2 (e5) then 4/4 (e8) for Microtubule stabilizers, with k-neighbors 6/10 stabilizers in both comparisons. I correctly weighted the unanimous NSC vote over the minority k-neighbor hits.
- Dose-response texture: tub_std rho=+1.00 p=0 (e10) across indices 0,3,5,7 showed monotonic texture/bundling increase. I did not over-weight tub_mean rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e9) - its plateau is expected for saturation and does not contradict stabilization; texture (std/contrast) is the more specific bundling readout.

What could have misled / trade-offs:
- k-neighbors included Microtubule destabilizers 2/10 (e5,e8) and Eg5 inhibitors 2/10 (e8), Protein synthesis 1/10 (e5). These share downstream mitotic defects like lower density (e4) and altered nuclear morphology (e6 nuc_solidity -13.3) that can mimic multinucleation/arrest. I ruled them out because destabilizers require tubulin loss/decrease in tub_mean/std, opposite to e2/e3/e7, and Eg5/Aurora inhibitors do not produce the extreme tubulin polymerization/bundling signal seen here.
- Single replicate per dose: each well was n=1 per dose (e2,e3,e6,e7), so formal within-dose variance could not be estimated. The decision to spend budget on dose coverage rather than replicates was justified here because effect sizes were huge (z ~+50-75) and consistent across four independent doses, making a replicate flip unlikely, as noted in review. With budget exhausted, no affordable discriminating follow-up remained.
- Low-dose act_mean z=+10.0 (e6) could have suggested actin modulation if viewed in isolation, but actin changes were an order of magnitude smaller than tubulin and not reproducible at higher doses where tubulin dominated, so I deprioritized it.

Lesson: for taxol-like stabilizers, tub_std and tub_glcm_contrast are more discriminating than tub_mean alone due to early saturation; combining high-dose maximal phenotype (e2), low-dose threshold (e6), visual bundling (e4), unanimous atlas NSC vote (e8), and monotonic texture dose-response (e10) was sufficient to separate stabilizers from destabilizers and mitotic kinase/kinesin inhibitors despite shared proliferation defects.
